item.title: Launch of the CEN Workshop 'UNITED CIRCLES - Feasibility to Finance Guidelines for Industrial-Urban Symbiosis within Hubs for Circularity'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being established to develop a CEN Workshop Agreement (CWA) entitled 'Feasibility to Finance Guidelines for Industrial-Urban Symbiosis within Hubs for Circularity: the UNITED CIRCLES Approach'. The Workshop stems from work being done in UNITED CIRCLES Horizon project aiming to provide practical guidance for advancing Industrial-Urban Symbiosis (IUS) from feasibility assessment to investment readiness. Industrial-Urban Symbiosis is increasingly recognized as a key enabler of the circular economy, supporting the recovery and valorisation of materials, energy, water and other resources through collaboration between industries, cities and local stakeholders. item.title: Europe’s competitiveness needs a stronger standardization system – not a fragmented one
item.description: Today, the European Commission published its proposal for the New Standardization Regulation, which would repeal Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012. CEN and CENELEC support the objective of making European standardization faster and more effective. However, several elements of the proposal risk weakening the very system it seeks to improve. Reform should strengthen, not fragment, the successful system Europe already has. For decades, this independent, consensus-based public-private partnership has brought together industry, SMEs, public authorities, consumers, researchers and societal stakeholders through national participation. item.title: New CEN Technical Specification Helps Turn Children’s Anthropometric Data into Better Design Decisions
item.description: A child seat that fits properly, a desk that supports a comfortable posture or protective equipment that allows freedom of movement all depend on good design decisions. These decisions require reliable data, but also an understanding of how factors such as age, posture, clothing and movement affect children’s dimensions in real-life situations. CEN/TS 18296-2:2026 bridges this gap, helping turn anthropometric and strength data into safer, more comfortable and more user-friendly products and environments for children. The recently published CEN/TS 18296-2:2026 provides guidance on the correct application of anthropometric and strength data for children in Europe. item.title: Launch of the CEN/CLC Workshop 'Battery2Life - Interoperable BMS principles'
item.description: A new CEN/CLC Workshop is being established to explore the options of second life batteries in the context of an interoperable Battery Management System (BMS). The Workshop stems from work being done in Battery2Life – a project aiming to bring innovation to the European battery industry. The Battery2Life project is concerned to answer the growing problem of the transition of batteries to their second life use. It recognises the need for more adaptable systems and smarter design, and the challenge of developing new methods for reconfiguration of used batteries in a way that is efficient and reliable. item.title: Call for Experts: Help Shape Europe's Future Standard for Transport Data Exchange
item.description: The European Commission, through the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA), is seeking experts to contribute to the development of the future harmonized EN 16614 Network Timetable Exchange (NeTEx) standard. This strategic initiative will support the implementation of key EU legislation on multimodal travel information and rail data interoperability, helping to build a more connected and digital European transport system. item.title: Improving protection for motorcycle police officers
item.description: Motorcycle protective clothing certified to the highest protection standard under the EN 17092 series is primarily designed with recreational riders in mind. However, whether this standard adequately addresses the elevated occupational hazards faced by professional riders, such as police officers, is a growing concern. Unlike leisure riders, motorcycle police officers operate routinely in high-risk environments, responding to emergencies, conducting escorts, and patrolling in all weather conditions. Under the Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Regulation, equipment must be suitable for the specific operational risks of the user. item.title: New European standard for learning towers adopted
item.description: ANEC welcomed the adoption of a new European Standard for learning towers, also known as ‘kitchen helpers’. EN 18122 ‘High chairs and learning towers – Learning towers – Requirements and test methods’ was developed by CEN/TC 364 ‘High chairs and learning towers’, following a proposal from ANEC. ANEC raised the issue in 2021, as their analysis suggested that the products themselves not only presented fall and entrapment (and possibly other) hazards, but could also give rise to hazards by providing access to dangers such as thermal injuries, lacerations and poisonings when used close to kitchen work surfaces and in bathrooms. item.title: Join an Academic Standards Day near you!
item.description: This autumn, EDU4Standards is bringing its Academic Standards Days to Ireland (15 October), Sweden (16 October), Belgium (26 October), Norway (18 November) and Finland (3 December). Designed for students, researchers, educators, and standards professionals, this series aims to increase interest and deepen the understanding of standardization within academia, laying the foundations to train a new generation of experts. Through presentations, panel discussions and workshops, participants will gain practical insights into standardization and connect with experts from academia, industry and the standards community.
